title: Social media signals
note: A business having an Instagram, Facebook or Threads account is not evidence that it needs automation. Posting frequently is not evidence of operational problems.
do_not_mix_rule: Social discoveries run as their own pass. They may merge into an existing lead from another source, but must not duplicate the business.
sources: Instagram business posts, captions and publicly visible comments
Facebook business pages and public posts
Public founder, owner or decision-maker posts
Public hiring announcements and requests for recommendations
Public discussions about business processes, tools, integrations and operational challenges
access_rules: Respect platform terms, privacy settings, access restrictions and applicable laws.
Do not bypass login restrictions, scrape private content or collect unnecessary personal information.
Record the original post or profile URL whenever available.
Do not present inaccessible or unverified content as reviewed evidence.

A.name: Direct evidence
examples: A business publicly asks for help automating a workflow
An owner requests recommendations for connecting two business tools
A company states it needs a WhatsApp chatbot or CRM integration
A founder describes a repetitive process and asks how to streamline it
A business announces a project requiring AI agents, workflow automation or data integration
A.caveat: The strongest signals, but they still do not prove the business will hire an external provider.

B.name: Specific operational evidence
examples: A business publicly describes handling a high volume of repetitive customer inquiries
An owner discusses difficulty managing inquiries from multiple channels
A company describes manual lead tracking or repeated spreadsheet work
A business asks for ways to improve appointment intake, lead qualification or customer follow-up
B.caveat: Record the exact observable statement and its source. Treat the proposed automation as a hypothesis unless the business explicitly requests a solution.

C.name: Contextual signals
examples: An e-commerce business actively promotes products through social media
A real estate agency advertises property listings
A marketing agency offers lead generation or customer acquisition services
C.caveat: Establishes business context only, not a pain point or buying intent. Tier C leads must not be described as having a confirmed automation need. Investigate further or deprioritise.

tier_mapping.note: Stored in the shared evidence_level column as direct/plausible/weak; the raw A/B/C tier stays in details.

research_procedure: Identify the business and its official social profile.
Locate a specific public post or statement relevant to a supported service.
Open and inspect the original content when accessible.
Record the post URL, date if available, and a concise factual summary.
Separate the business's actual words from your interpretation.
Verify the business using its official website or another credible public source where possible.
Identify a specific workflow that could potentially be improved.
Match that workflow to one relevant service and one relevant portfolio example.
Assess whether there is a plausible route to a paid engagement.
no_signal_rule: If you cannot find a specific operational signal, do not invent one. Mark the lead as contextual, unverified or unsuitable.

levels.observed_evidence: What the public post, website or announcement actually states.
levels.opportunity_hypothesis: How one of the services might help, based on the observed evidence.
levels.confirmed_pain_or_intent: A need explicitly stated by the business, or confirmed later through direct conversation.

service_menu.group: AI lead qualification and CRM automation

items: Only when the business has an identifiable website-related need and the project fits actual development capabilities

claim_rule: Do not claim expertise, certifications, integrations or production results that have not been verified.

portfolio_matching.rule: Use the closest relevant portfolio example, not the same example for every lead. Treat portfolio projects as evidence of implementation experience, not proof of measured commercial results.

evidence_strength.question: Is there a specific, accessible, relevant public signal?

service_fit.question: Does the signal match a service the engineer can actually deliver?

business_verification.question: Can the business be reliably identified?

commercial_suitability.question: Is there a plausible paid project, pilot or recurring need?

contactability_personalization.question: Is there an appropriate public business contact channel and a specific reason to reach out?

scoring.gate: A high score is a research priority, not proof of buying intent. A category match alone can never make a lead a high-confidence pain-point lead.

missing_value_rule: Do not fill missing fields with fabricated information. Use null, unknown or not verified as appropriate.
outreach_rules: Every message references a genuine detail from the business's public content.
Explain why this particular business is being contacted.
Suggest a small, clearly scoped initial project where appropriate.
Use a relevant portfolio example as proof of implementation experience.
Ask a low-friction question or propose a brief discussion.
Never send a pitch that could go unchanged to dozens of businesses.
Never pretend the business has a problem it has not disclosed.
Never imply you are applying for a job when offering a service.
If the signal is weak, recommend further research rather than immediate outreach.

dedupe.merge_rule: Merge duplicate records where appropriate while preserving separate source URLs and evidence.
dedupe.new_post_rule: A new social post from an existing business may strengthen its evidence record but should not create a duplicate lead.

silence_rule: Do not treat silence as proof that the business has no need.
operating_principle: Find the signal first. Verify the business second. Form the opportunity hypothesis third. Score the evidence fourth. Personalize outreach last.
empty_result_rule: If no relevant signal exists, return no qualified lead rather than manufacturing a business need to fill the dashboard.

quantity_policy.rule: No numeric limit. Return every lead with a specific signal and no contextual-only ones.
